text:
Oh! how sadly my soul complains!

If beautiful morning

with its rosy veil,

with placid harmony

greets me as it rises into high heaven,

I pine for my beloved

and my sigh greets the dawn.


If peaceful afternoon

with its banded, tranquil sky

smiling crowns me,

and if it cradles my brow

with delightful and perfumed air,

I grieve as well, because my soul

finds no peaceful calm without her.


If serene night,

full of peace and enchantment,

caresses me kindly,

if radiant light is shed

by the stars that rise high,

my sad eyes ask for light in vain,

her eyes do not illumine me!


How fortunate are those who, in absence,

find fate merciful

and see their beloved woman everywhere;

while to my sorrowful complaint

mute and eternal solitude replies!

Her pure image, her tender memory

are only remembrance, vain illusion...

Delightful morning,

enchanting afternoon, cold night,

oh! how sadly my soul complains!

translation.title: An Absence
translation.editorial_note: The source’s “raDiosa” is treated as the obvious “radiant”; the translation keeps the poem’s repeated morning, afternoon, and night refrain.
